PullRequest.Title: copilot: apply the CopilotCliCommand policy to Linux packages and the macOS shim
PullRequest.Body:

Addresses microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10108. Builds on @DonJayamanne's #342014 (merged in here with its commits) and ports the macOS reader from his #341916.

## Summary

The `CopilotCliCommand` policy now governs the `copilot` command at install time on Linux and in the shim on every platform, matching Windows setup:

| `CopilotCliCommand` = false | Windows | Linux DEB/RPM | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Don't expose `copilot` on PATH, and remove what VS Code added | Setup (existing) | **`/usr/bin/copilot` not created; a link to either edition's shim is removed** on install, upgrade, reconfigure, and removal | VS Code doesn't create a link (unchanged) |
| Don't install Copilot CLI | Setup + shim (existing) | Shim (from #342014) | **Shim reads the policy** (configuration-profile domains of all qualities) |
| Integrated terminals | Copilot extension (existing) | Same | Same |

- **`copilot --vscode-shim policy`**: exits `0` (allowed) or `10` (disabled) using the shim's platform reader, so package scripts don't parse `policy.json` in shell. Any other exit (missing shim, older shim → `2`) is treated as unknown.
- **`copilot-link.sh`**: `install` queries the edition's shim. Disabled → withdraw a link to either edition's shim (foreign entries are preserved). Unknown → warn and leave the entry unchanged (never create a link). `remove` queries the remaining edition's shim and hands the link over only when that edition is usable, wants the command, and the policy allows it.
- **DEB opt-out**: new `<package>/add-copilot-command` debconf question (boolean, default `true`, **medium** priority so normal installs don't prompt), asked only by `code` and `code-insiders`. Admins can preseed it (`echo "code code/add-copilot-command boolean false" | sudo debconf-set-selections`); `dpkg-reconfigure code` asks it and re-applies the policy. RPM has no equivalent; the policy is the only control there.
- **macOS shim**: `CFPreferencesCopyAppValue` for `com.microsoft.VSCode`, `…VSCodeInsiders`, `…VSCodeExploration`, `com.visualstudio.code.oss`; only `CFBoolean false` disables, any quality wins (same rule as Windows). New target-specific dependency `core-foundation-sys 0.8.7`.
- Policy description and `policyData.jsonc` now mention the Linux packages; REQUIREMENTS.md documents the ordering (policy → debconf answer → install), the `policy` command, and how to re-apply a changed policy before the next upgrade (`dpkg-reconfigure` / RPM reinstall).

Policy changes made after installation apply on the next upgrade or reconfiguration. Until then a leftover link still can't install Copilot CLI, because the shim enforces the policy at runtime.

## Validation

| Environment | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Windows x64, Rust stable | `cargo test --locked --manifest-path copilot_shim/Cargo.toml` | Passed (69 lib + integration) |
| Windows, Rust stable | `cargo clippy --manifest-path copilot_shim/Cargo.toml --target {aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu} --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`; Windows `--lib --test app` | Passed |
| `rust:1.88` container (CI toolchain) | `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` | Passed (72 lib tests; native policy test ignored as designed) |
| `rust:1.88` container | `cargo clippy --target {aarch64,x86_64}-apple-darwin --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` | Passed (macOS tests not executed) |
| Linux release shim | `copilot --vscode-shim policy` with no/disabled/malformed policy and an extra option | `0` / `10` / `0` / `2` |
| `node:24-bookworm-slim` | `npm run test-copilot-shim-helper` (new) | Passed: 6 tests under `dash` and `bash`; all 6 fail against the helper from #342014 |
| `node:24-bookworm-slim`, then Windows after 8d36014c6c2 | `npm run test-copilot-shim-rendering` | Passed. It now has 2 tests, which check the real helper source and templates; the 4 that only exercised the harness validator were removed in review |
| `debian:stable-slim`, real `dpkg`/debconf | Minimal `code`/`code-insiders` DEBs rendered from the real templates and shim: pre-staged policy, upgrade, `dpkg-reconfigure`, preseeded opt-out, two-edition hand-over, foreign command, purge | Passed: 20 scenarios; under a pseudo-TTY a default-priority install doesn't prompt, `dpkg-reconfigure` asks and applies the answer, and `dpkg-reconfigure code-exploration` doesn't ask |
| `fedora:latest` | RPM `%post`/`%postun` rendered from the spec template, run as rpm does | Passed: 9 scenarios |
| Repository | `npm run export-policy-data` | Only the `CopilotCliCommand` description changed |
| Repository | `npm run eslint -- <changed TS>`, `npm run precommit -- <changed files>` | Passed |

### Product build validation

Unpublished product builds of this branch (`VSCODE_PUBLISH=false`, `VSCODE_RELEASE=false`):

| Build | Contents | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [485321](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=485321) | Insiders: Linux x64 (DEB, RPM, snap) and macOS arm64, with tests and artifact sanity tests | Passed: unit, integration, smoke, browser/remote, Copilot shim tests on Linux, and artifact sanity tests on Linux and macOS |
| [485326](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=485326) | Stable: Linux x64, tests skipped (same commit as 485321) | Linux stage passed. The build failed only at the Stable-only `APIScan` stage's production-readiness checkpoint, which doesn't touch Linux packaging |
| [485379](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=485379) | Insiders: macOS x64 CLI only, to run the shim's Rust tests on macOS (the arm64 CLI job doesn't run them) | `Test Copilot shim`, `Lint Copilot shim` (clippy), and formatting passed on macOS, including the macOS policy reader's tests. The rest of the build was canceled afterwards |

Real packages from these builds, installed with the system package manager in clean containers:

| Environment | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `ubuntu:24.04`, `apt` | Insiders DEB: disabled policy staged before install creates no link and the shipped shim's `--vscode-shim policy` exits `10`; `dpkg-reconfigure` after lifting it creates the link, `copilot --vscode-shim policy` exits `0`, `copilot` without Copilot CLI or a terminal prints the not-found message and exits `127`; reinstall with a disabled policy removes the link; preseeded `false` gives it up and `true` restores it; disabled policy keeps a foreign `/usr/bin/copilot`; remove deletes the link; purge drops the question | 13 checks passed |
| `fedora:latest`, `dnf` | Insiders RPM: the same for install, reinstall, and remove | 7 checks passed |
| `ubuntu:24.04` and `fedora:latest` | Stable and Insiders packages from the same commit: install Insiders, install Stable (takeover), reinstall Insiders (takeover), remove the owner (hand-over to Stable), remove the non-owner, remove the last edition; no `vscode_copilot_link` warnings, and `copilot` works whenever an edition is installed | 7 steps passed with `apt` and with `dnf` |

### Validation limits

- Don's full package-lifecycle matrix (`npm run test-copilot-shim`) wasn't run. The real-package checks above cover its main ownership cases and the new policy cases.
- No real macOS configuration profile or `cfprefsd` propagation test; TPI microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10123 covers it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke `copilot` when an eligible Copilot CLI is already installed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shim performs its existing PATH and official-install-directory discovery, then immediately execs/supervises the discovered CLI. `prepare_workflow` returns before `request_install`, so the new Linux policy-file and macOS preferences readers are off this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect PATH candidates and the supported fallback installation directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass over distinct PATH directories plus at most one fallback directory; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same candidate discovery occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before selecting and launching the real CLI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace/supervise the shim with the selected Copilot CLI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same final launch occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the requested product execution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct PATH directories, unchanged by the diff; the added package symlink only makes the existing shim available system-wide.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous shim process followed by one final CLI process; no fan-out or added parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovery is intentionally per invocation and has no cross-process cache. The new policy readers are not reached after a successful candidate discovery.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: control flow returns a launch action before any policy call, as corroborated by the added policy-read tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem timing varies with PATH composition, but the diff adds no work to this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: normal launches of an installed CLI do not pay the new policy-read cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke `copilot` when no eligible CLI is installed, including macOS interactive installation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After existing PATH and fallback discovery miss, the shim synchronously reads policy. Linux reads and parses `/etc/vscode/policy.json` once; macOS performs up to four CFPreferences reads and stops at the first disabling value. If allowed, the existing prompt/download/installer workflow proceeds; if disabled, the new check short-circuits that expensive work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the Linux policy JSON file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read per fresh missing-CLI invocation that reaches an installation decision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Non-Windows shims returned `false` without reading a policy file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous before prompting or starting an installer; a disabled policy avoids all later network and subprocess work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query effective preferences for Stable, Insiders, Exploration, and OSS domains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One to four synchronous preference lookups, stopping when a false boolean is found.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The macOS shim did not read native policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous before installation, but bounded to four scalar local lookups.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/download the Copilot CLI installer or release payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing serial route/fallback behavior; zero calls when policy disables installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Allowed missing-CLI invocations already used these network routes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing dominant installation work after consent/policy allows it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run curl/wget and then the downloaded Bash installer on Unix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bounded serial attempts; Linux now avoids the prior extra PATH-filter discovery before Bash.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same installer subprocesses ran before; Linux previously prepared a filtered PATH first.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing installation critical path when policy allows installation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Linux parsing scales with policy-file bytes; macOS remains fixed at four domains. Realistic policy files are small, and the path is reached only after CLI discovery misses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shim process; policy reads are serial and bounded. Existing downloader and installer subprocesses remain serial fallback routes rather than concurrent fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Policy is deliberately uncached so each process observes administrator changes. Linux failures/missing/invalid JSON fail open; macOS values are copied and released per query. No shared cache misses or retained keys are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new local reads and their placement are explicit in `request_install`, setup probe/install, and policy tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact local read latency is platform-dependent, but the bounded work is small relative to a missing-CLI prompt/download and can remove that work under a disabled policy.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added synchronous work is bounded policy enforcement on the missing-CLI path and can suppress much larger existing installer work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install, upgrade, reconfigure, or remove VS Code DEB/RPM packages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Package-manager lifecycle scripts run the embedded helper synchronously. The helper checks link state, invokes an edition shim in `--vscode-shim policy` mode, and performs guarded local link mutation. Package configuration/removal waits for these steps.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the packaged Rust shim to evaluate native policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch for ordinary install/remove; up to two fixed launches when ownership is released or handed over between the two editions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Package lifecycle scripts did not query Copilot shim policy or manage `/usr/bin/copilot`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Package configuration/removal waits for the bounded local process exits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat/readlink the shared entry and atomically create, replace, or remove a recognized symlink using a temporary sibling directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed number of operations against `/usr/bin/copilot` and at most two known edition targets per hook.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shared Copilot command link was managed by these package hooks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous but bounded local filesystem work in package lifecycle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: resources/linux/debian/postinst.template and postrm.template via debconf `db_input`, `db_go`, and `db_get`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or apply the DEB add-command preference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed question/query for Stable or Insiders; OSS and unrecognized editions no-op.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Copilot command debconf preference existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of DEB configuration/removal; normal installs use the default at medium priority.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed edition set of two and one shared link, independent of package payload size or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Package hooks are serialized by the package manager. Each helper call launches one policy shim normally and at most two in hand-over paths; no unbounded concurrency or per-file fan-out exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each package hook re-reads policy and debconf state so upgrades/reconfiguration apply current administrator choices. There is no long-lived process or retained cache; hand-over is limited to two known editions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper control flow, templates, and lifecycle tests establish exact subprocess and filesystem cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Process startup and package-manager baseline duration vary, but added work is fixed and rare compared with package installation/removal itself.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the feature necessarily adds bounded local work to infrequent package hooks without collection scaling, network access, or concurrency bursts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build Linux packages and explicitly run the focused package lifecycle fixture suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Gulp packaging module reads the helper once and embeds it into generated scripts. The opt-in fixture generator serially invokes existing production prepare/build tasks for declared source copies; the isolated lifecycle suite serially runs package-manager transactions selected by an explicit Mocha grep.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read `resources/linux/copilot-link.sh` once when the Linux packaging Gulp file is loaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small source-file read per packaging task process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The helper source was not loaded or embedded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run production Gulp prepare/build tasks and package metadata tools for explicitly listed fixtures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two package-task subprocesses per declared entry/format plus fixed metadata/package creation calls; opt-in only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This focused fixture generator did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Critical only to explicit fixture generation, not product or default sanity execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run dpkg/rpm transactions and bounded package inspection queries for selected lifecycle scenarios.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed by the explicitly selected test matrix; Mocha bails on first failure and retries are disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The focused lifecycle suite did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Critical only to the dedicated isolated test command.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicitly declared fixture entries/formats and selected test scenarios; neither runs implicitly in product or the default sanity runner.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Generation and lifecycle tests are intentionally serial to preserve package state and hook ordering; no background burst is introduced. They are separate from normal product startup and the default sanity runner.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Generated fixture manifests and packages are persisted artifacts; test runs validate hashes rather than download/discover fixtures. No product cache is affected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: scripts and documentation require explicit commands and fixture manifests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Full package builds can be lengthy, but this is deliberate offline test generation rather than a user-facing regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance finding: expensive work is explicit test/build infrastructure, bounded by supplied fixtures and excluded from normal runtime paths.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 39 changed files and every diff page. Traced normal and missing CLI launch paths, macOS/Linux policy readers, DEB/RPM package lifecycle hooks, installer subprocesses, and the opt-in fixture tooling. Added runtime work is bounded and either off the installed-CLI path or limited to infrequent package/install workflows; no high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
